title: Riau-Lingga Sultanate
capsule: The Riau-Lingga Sultanate was a Malay-Bugis polity governing the Riau and Lingga archipelagos south of the Malay Peninsula, constituted in its definitive form by the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 which partitioned the former Johor-Riau Sultanate between British and Dutch spheres. Authority was shared between the Malay sultan based at Daik on Lingga and a Bugis Yang Dipertuan Muda (underking), and the sultanate functioned as a Dutch protectorate until 1911. The last sultan, Abdul Rahman II, was deposed on 11 February 1911 when the Dutch dissolved the sultanate after he declined to sign a new treaty; he died in exile in Singapore in 1930. The territory corresponds to today's Riau Islands Province of Indonesia.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The sultanate's island territories are clearly identified in Dutch colonial administrative records and the 1824 treaty; the atlas start date of 1820 reflects pre-treaty developments rather than the formal 1824 partition.
